name: Roaring Token
reason: The source term 'Roaring Token' (also rendered 'Roaring Command' in the translation) was kept nearly verbatim, as it already fits the Western fantasy register.
description: A rare and extremely expensive communication artifact of the Upper Realm, crafted from the throat of a Roaring Celestial Tapir. A single broadcast through a Roaring Token echoes through every corner of existence, letting Supreme Lords trade words across the universe and letting leaders summon hundreds of followers at once. Zane uses his Roaring Token for years to speak with a mysterious singer in a distant, ethereal world, and such tokens feature prominently in the late-series universe-spanning arcs (Eps 991-1309).

name: Freya
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Mu Mingxue' was fully localized to 'Freya', a graceful Western name fitting a refined young woman of the Upper Realm; no surname was assigned in the delivered episodes.
description: A young woman who ascended to the Upper Realm around the same time as Zane and worked beside him in the Sovereign Stone mines (Eps 1006-1206). Her uncle is the city lord of a major city in the Spirit Martial Holy Land, and she initially sought refuge with him before he proved treacherous; Zane later confronts the uncle when Freya calls for help via her Message Rune ('That's your uncle?' - Ep 1117). She is nearly used as a 'human cauldron' for another's training before Zane intervenes. Matches source character Mu Mingxue, whose uncle-city-lord storyline (chs 986-1186) aligns exactly with Freya's episodes.

name: Fiona
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Huo Yun'er' was fully localized to 'Fiona', a regal Western name suiting a Divine Kingdom princess.
description: A princess of the Wind Divine Kingdom (source: Heavenly Wind / Tianfeng Divine Kingdom) featured in Eps 813-1037. Direct and polite despite her royal status, she first meets Zane during the Divine Kingdom arc and spars with him early on, rarely getting the chance to truly let loose as a princess (Ep 815). Her status is higher than an ordinary Crown Prince's, and she is counted among the great geniuses of the Divine Kingdoms. Matches source character Huo Yun'er, princess of the Tianfeng Divine Nation (chs 791-1014), whose sparring introduction mirrors Fiona's.

name: Cloud Road
reason: The source trial 'Road of Trials' (also translated 'Trial Taker's Road'), administered by the Cloud Hall, was renamed 'Cloud Road' to tie the trial directly to Cloud Hall in a compact Western fantasy name.
description: A prestigious multi-stage trial dimension opened by Cloud Hall for elite disciples, serving as the gateway to becoming a Cloud Hall elite (Eps 189-1013, core arc around Eps 231-400). Only top finishers of sect competitions earn the right to attempt it; disciples of the Thirty-Three Peaks are effectively shut out. Per the master sheet it contains the Sea of Raging Fire, cliff challenges, Hidden Tests, the Death Road, the Thrilling Icy Plain, and Sixth-Grade Sect ruins, and is entered via a gateway powered by Supreme Vitality crystals. Corresponds to the source novel's Road of Trials / Trial Taker's Road under the Cloud Hall (chs ~344-700).

name: Dustin Blackwood
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Zhang Wuxian' was fully localized to 'Dustin'; the surname 'Blackwood' was assigned to render his wealthy merchant family (source Zhang Family) as House Blackwood, keeping a consistent family unit.
description: A scion of House Blackwood, the wealthy merchant house whose business dealings span the entire Capital, and a loyal early friend of Zane (Eps 59-973). He knows most of the big players in the Capital's commerce and helps Zane navigate auctions and house politics, including the feud with Felix. The master sheet notes he is close to Ingrid. Matches source character Zhang Wuxian of the Zhang Family, the wealthiest family behind the Tianlu Auction House, whose chapter range (43-950) and all-male pronoun profile align with Dustin's.

name: War Sage
reason: The source rank 'Battle Saint' (also rendered 'Battle-Saint'/'War Saint', i.e. the Life and Death Realm) was localized as 'War Sage' to fit the adaptation's Western fantasy rank naming.
description: A high cultivation rank on the main continent (Eps 568-954), sitting just below the Soul Sea Realm masters and forming the true backbone of any real fighting force. Reaching it requires surviving a heavenly tribulation. War Sages of every race appear around the Tower of Sin and Cursed Land arcs, including Ogre and Demon Race War Sages whom Zane confronts. Corresponds to the source's Battle Saint / Life and Death Realm (chs ~553-930).

name: Sloane Kincaid
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Ji Luoxue' was fully localized to 'Sloane', a sleek, formidable Western name for a top female genius; the surname 'Kincaid' was assigned to replace the source's Ji Family name.
description: A supremely talented female warrior who duels Zane in the Illusory Battlefield arc (Eps 1231-1312), introduced in her own title episode (Ep 1231) wearing a purple silk robe with an ivory ribbon in her long black hair. She fights with golden wind techniques, dissolving into the wind itself, commands clones, and withstands Zane's Nether God Shadows with casual composure, tapping artifacts like a ring on her thumb mid-battle. Matches source character Ji Luoxue of the Ji Family (chs 1211-1306), a genius whose clones alone fight the Ji prodigies to a draw.

name: Spatial Law
reason: The source term 'Law of Space' (also 'Space Law') was localized as 'Spatial Law(s)' for smoother English phrasing in the adaptation.
description: One of the rarest and most powerful of all Laws, governing perception and manipulation of space itself; it is counted with the Law of Time as the most mysterious of the Laws. Zane gains his first insight into the Spatial Laws after surviving a voidstorm (Eps 352-353), letting him perceive exact dimensions and spatial properties - an ability so rare that even masters like Kenneth and Eddy never learned it, and most refuse to believe he has it. Comprehension of its levels underpins spatial travel and advanced techniques, and it remains relevant through the late series (Eps 353-1255). Corresponds to the source's Law of Space (chs 344-1235).

name: Saul
reason: The source character 'Afo', the puppet steward of the Immortal's Mansion, was localized as 'Saul', an old-fashioned Western name fitting an ancient, lonely guardian.
description: The ancient guardian of the Elysian Keep - a puppet given life by a human soul and bound to the Keep for thousands of years (introduced Ep 157, recurring through Ep 1199). Desperately lonely, he created puppet companions for himself and pushes Zane to take the Keep's master's test, promising to save him if he fails. He becomes Zane's guide to the Keep's tokens and treasures. Matches source character Afo, whose puppet body was created by the first master of the Immortal's Mansion (chs 143-1179).

name: Harlen Divine Kingdom
reason: The source's 'Black Iron Divine Kingdom' (also 'Black Iron Divine Nation') was renamed the 'Harlen Divine Kingdom', giving the kingdom a Western dynastic name instead of the literal Chinese metal epithet.
description: One of the four great Divine Kingdoms of the Divine Kingdom continent (Eps 782-1001), alongside the Wind and Star Field Divine Kingdoms and War Emperor York's domain. Zane competes for its Harlen Token and fights as its champion, and its Emperor watches the mass ascension of his Soul Sea Realm masters to the Upper World with dread (Eps 1000-1001). Prince Randy is among its royals. Corresponds to the source's Black Iron Divine Kingdom, the Zhou family's realm (chs ~758-978).

name: Harlen Emperor
reason: The source character Zhou Huang, emperor of the Black Iron Divine Kingdom, is referred to by his title; the title was localized as 'Harlen Emperor' to match the kingdom's new name.
description: The ruling Emperor of the Harlen Divine Kingdom (Eps 807-1003), a Soul Sea Realm-era monarch who clashes verbally with War Emperor York and whose authority Zane openly defies. Matches source character Zhou Huang, emperor of the Zhou family's Black Iron Divine Kingdom (chs ~777-980), who claims Luo Zheng as his kingdom's champion.

name: Harlen Token
reason: The source's 'Dark Iron Token' / 'Iron Token' of the Black Iron Divine Kingdom was renamed 'Harlen Token' to match the kingdom's localized name.
description: A coveted credential of the Harlen Divine Kingdom (Eps 783-792), earned through a competitive test; for the kingdom's warriors it is everything, and elimination means losing the chance for good. Zane enters the test and is personally offered one by a master impressed by his strength. Corresponds to the source's Iron Token / Dark Iron Token of the Black Iron Divine Kingdom (chs ~764-766).

name: Mist Palace
reason: The source's 'Misty Cloud Palace' (also rendered 'Cloud Mist Heavenly Palace') was shortened to 'Mist Palace' for the Western fantasy register.
description: A great power of the Upper Realm where Zane trains and rises after his ascension (Eps 1040-1320), traditionally gathering thousands of genius warriors. It is where Zane is tested with the Red Cloud Ring, where news of his skill displays spreads like wildfire, and its warriors - including talents like Jasper and Layla - follow the Illusory Battlefield ranking pyramid. Corresponds to the source's Misty Cloud Palace / Cloud Mist Heavenly Palace (chs ~995-1300), one of the Thirteen Palaces led by Yun Luo's faction.

name: Celestial Essence
reason: The source material 'Heaven's Divination Essence' (also translated 'Heaven Amplification Essence' / 'Sky Derivation Essence') was renamed 'Celestial Essence', a cleaner name for the Western fantasy setting.
description: A precious liquid material produced when the Cobalt Dragon's Black Fire smelts down weapons - a high-grade weapon yields around five drops (first featured Eps 99-100, recurring through Ep 1236). It vanishes if the weapon is destroyed by ordinary means, is unknown to standard forging texts, and commands insane prices at auction, where Great Houses bid fortunes for it. It can be fused into weapons to forcibly raise their grade and is fed to the Cobalt Dragon to light its scales. Corresponds to the source's Heaven's Divination Essence obtained by Luo Zheng's black flame (chs ~86-1143).

name: Mythic Weapon
issues: Name drift: Eps 251-450 used the deprecated 'Mystic Weapon' for this tier (per master sheet); 'Mythic Weapon' is canonical per show decision for Eps 451+. 'Legendary Weapon' was also an Ep 4 error for the tier name.
reason: The source tier 'Xuan Weapon' (rendered 'mystic weapon' in parts of the translation) was localized as 'Mythic Weapon', the canonical Tier-3 weapon name in the show's weapon hierarchy.
description: The Tier-3 weapon grade in the show's hierarchy (above Spirit Weapon at tier 2, below Sacred Arms at tier 4), appearing from Ep 193 through Ep 1130. Forging one requires deciphering Celestial Law, and most smiths sacrifice decades merely to glimpse one; Zane's crafting of a genuine Mythic Weapon (Ep 218) stuns master smith Harrison. Mythic weapons can last for millennia, and Zane's father once wielded a top-tier Mythic sword, the Green Wind-Rider Sword. Corresponds to the source's Xuan Weapon grade.

name: Mythic Sigil
reason: Named in parallel with the Mythic Weapon tier: the inscription-grade above a Spirit Glyph was localized as 'Mythic Sigil' to keep the tier vocabulary consistent.
description: A weapon inscription far rarer than a Spirit Glyph, which Zane identifies on a blade during the Mythic Weapon forging arc (Eps 218-223). No specific source term is attested in the evidence, but the concept follows the source's weapon-rune tiers.

name: Slade
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Ming Dao' was fully localized to 'Slade', a harsh-sounding Western name fitting a sneering antagonist.
description: A sneering, sadistic antagonist of the final delivered arc in the Illusory Battlefield (Eps 1307-1321), who leads a crew of cackling followers and holds a mysterious grip over a woman who endures his behavior. He mocks his opponents as cowards and rats before Zane's group confronts him. Matches source character Ming Dao (chs 1287-1301), the arrogant son of Heavenly Sovereign Broken Shadow, who demands enemies kneel and be killed repeatedly in the Illusory Battlefield and whom Phantom quietly despises while enduring him.

name: Sovereign Stone
reason: The source's 'Zhen Yuanyu' (true origin jade), the precious stone mined and spent in the Upper Realm, was localized as 'Sovereign Stone' to convey its supreme grade without pinyin.
description: The most valuable grade of cultivation stone in the Upper Realm (Eps 1007-1290), ranking above top-grade and supreme stones and rare enough that a whole haul may not contain a single one. New ascenders like Zane dig them by hand in the mines, and they function as elite currency - buying residences, bidding for swords, and powering artifacts. Corresponds to the source's Zhen Yuanyu, which ascenders mine in the Spirit Martial Holy Land's pitch-black mountain ranges (chs 984-1270).

name: War General
reason: The source rank 'War General' was kept verbatim, as it already fits the Western fantasy register of the main continent's rank system.
description: A cultivation rank used on the main continent (Eps 564-951), equivalent to the Heartlands' Inner-Core Realm (source: Divine Core) and sitting below War Lords and the War Sages. War Generals of every race - human, Ogre, Demon Night - appear throughout the Tower of Sin arc, where even a 'mere' War General like the ogre Boris can outrank many War Lords in status. Corresponds verbatim to the source's War General rank on the Sea Dragon Continent (chs ~554-631).

name: Law
reason: The source's umbrella concept of 'Laws' (Law of Fire, Law of Space, etc.) was kept verbatim as the adaptation's term for the fundamental forces of cultivation.
description: The fundamental forces of the universe that cultivators comprehend to advance - Fire, Space, Time, the Five Elements and other Original Laws (Eps 267-1283). The better one understands a Law, the higher one's soul can climb; Law Obelisks let warriors study and test their comprehension, and nearly every movement art in the universe draws its power from some Law. Each Law Zane masters becomes another weapon in his arsenal. Corresponds directly to the source's Laws (Law of Fire, Law of Space, Law of Time, etc.).

name: Emperor
reason: Generic title referring to many different rulers across the series (Emperor Amos, the Empire's Emperor, the Harlen Emperor, Divine Emperors, etc.), not a single entity; specific emperors are tracked under their own names.

name: Frank
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Zhuo Bufan' was fully localized to 'Frank', a blunt, confident Western name fitting a proud top disciple; his father was separately localized as Emanuel Drew.
description: A top disciple of Cloud Hall and one of Zane's chief rivals in the Cloud Road era (Eps 367-990), son of Emanuel Drew and engaged to Lois, Lady Sigmund's prized disciple. Called 'a real dragon among men,' he wields a white spear with techniques like Sky-Breaking Thrust, Maelstrom Spear and Blood-Dragon Spear, ultimately achieving the Apex of Spear Intent. Proud and calculating, he initially sees Zane as beneath him before being forced to recognize his power. Matches source character Zhuo Bufan (chs 354-695), the white-spear genius with perfected Spear Intent whose father is 'Mister Zhuo.'

name: Oracle City
reason: The source's 'Tianqi City' (tianqi = 'apocalypse/heaven's revelation', also rendered 'Apocalypse City' and 'Heavenly Awakening City' in the translation) was localized as 'Oracle City', preserving the 'revelation' sense in a Western name.
description: A major commercial city in the Heartlands and seat of the World Merchants' Guild (Eps 441-1029). It hosts the great open Martial Tournament proposed by the Guild and is home to the Dragon Soar Arena, which becomes the city's focal point after Tia's arrival; Zane shops its bustling markets for supplies between Cloud Hall stints. Corresponds to the source's Tianqi City, the Central Domain's capital of commerce where the World Business Alliance holds its Martial Arts Conference (chs 428-1006).
